summary: Tenant ghosting and burst fractionation causing reserved-pool thinness and degraded throughput
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Streamline AI) reports periodic sharp drops in effective throughput for their dedicated reserved pool during midday burst windows. Symptoms look like the pool loses available GPU slots for short intervals (~30s–3m), causing request queuing and fallback to lower-capacity variants. Impact: increased P50 by ~2x and p99 by ~4x for embedding and short-chat routes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency spikes and request retries for production embeddings route.
- Autoscaler shows brief undershoots (no scale-up) during rapid client cohort activations.
- Billing credits are at risk due to SLA exposure if not mitigated.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved capacity (customer-dedicated) in prod-us-east.
- Affected routes: embeddings-short, chat-stream-compact.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Customer launches a scheduled analytics job that fans out many short-lived connections (~1000/min) from a small cohort of workers.
2) Within 30–90s, scheduler logs show many ephemeral sessions; allocator reports slot reservations but then quickly releases.
3) Autoscaler telemetry shows a short drop in GPU attachment rate and then a delayed scale-up.
4) Requests either queue (increasing p50) or fallback to pinned model variant with lower throughput.

Relevant logs / dashboards (high-level):
- Dedicated pool GPU attach rate: https://dash.redwood/prod-us-east/pool/streamline/attach-rate (spike-to-zero traces)
- Autoscaler events: https://dash.redwood/prod-us-east/autoscaler/events?range=last24h (backoff and retry hysteresis entries)
- Metrics: pool_free_slots, attach_latency_ms, prefetch_wait_count, kv_cache_size

Initial hypothesis:
- "Tenant ghosting": a cohort of ephemeral connections holds soft socket leases and heartbeats, causing the allocator to fragment GPU slots (fractionation) and under-report usable capacity to the autoscaler.
- Short-lived burst traffic causes the autoscaler to under-react due to smoothing windows and telemetry aggregation lag.
- Possible interaction with a new telemetry emitter that batches sidecar metrics, causing transient IO pressure on GPU attach path.

Customer notes (from initial contact):
- They see failures mostly between 11:45–12:30 UTC when their analytics cluster runs scheduled microjobs.
- They attempted to lower concurrency per worker, which reduced but did not eliminate the drop.

Requested next steps from customer:
- Temporary mitigation to avoid p99 regressions for the next two business days.
- Postmortem and recommended config changes to autoscale and prefetch settings.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Ticket opened after customer Slack (channel #support-streamline) reporting throughput collapse. Attached initial metrics and asked for sample request IDs.
2026-03-12 10:22 - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Ack. Pulling pool attach traces and autoscaler logs. Noted repeated attach latency spikes at 11:47 UTC. Creating debugging slice.

2026-03-12 13:15 - Riley Chen (Solutions Eng): Confirmed customer traffic pattern: ~1k short-lived embed calls/min from a job cluster. Suggested temporary concurrency cap on their side and increased keepalive time to reduce churn.

2026-03-13 09:04 - Jordan Myers (Runtime Eng): Found 3x increase in sidecar metric flushes correlated with attach latency. Raising hypothesis: sidecar emitter burst causes NVMe IO contention during attach window. Linked PR to throttle emitter. See PR #209.
2026-03-13 11:50 - Streamline AI (Customer): Applied temporary cap and observed reduced p99 but still saw p50 increase. Asking for platform-side mitigation while they plan a code change.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Deployed autoscaler smoothing override for Streamline reserved pool (shorten smoothing window, raise quickscale threshold). Monitoring impact.
investigation_notes: Collected attach traces from 2026-03-11T11:30–12:15 UTC; observed attach_latency_ms 95th at 2.3s (baseline 0.1s).
Prefetch_wait_count spikes line up with drop in pool_free_slots; kv_cache_size remains stable -> not pure cache OOM.
Reproduced ephemeral connection fanout in staging with synthetic client: created 1200 short-lived streams/min; allocator reported slot fragmentation within 45s.
Checked kernel metrics: NVMe queue depth elevated during incident windows, driver IO latencies spiked. Evidence suggests sidecar-batched metric flushes congesting host IO path.
Confirmed autoscaler telemetry lag: metric ingestion pipeline sampled every 60s; smoothing window 90s -> scale decisions missed bursts.

Related logs: runtime attach errors (attach_timeout) correlate with sidecar-flush timestamps. Grepped for 'attach_timeout' in runtime logs: https://logs.redwood/prod/query?term=attach_timeout&pool=streamline
Experiment: throttled sidecar emitter in a canary pool; attach_latency 95th dropped to 0.18s and pool_free_slots stabilized.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-14 08:30): modified autoscaler smoothing for Streamline pool (smoothing window reduced to 30s, quickscale threshold lowered). Immediate p50 drop observed; p99 improved after emitter throttle.
Hotfix: deployed temporary throttle for sidecar metric emitter on customer-adjacent hosts to reduce NVMe IO spikes. Canary validation shows stable attach path.
Customer workaround: reduce per-worker ephemeral connection churn and increase keepalive to 45s (recommended). Streamline confirmed reduced retries after change.
Follow-ups assigned: Jordan Myers to submit permanent fix to sidecar emitter (github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/209) to implement backpressure and adaptive flush windows.
Post-incident actions: create runbook entry for 'ephemeral-fanout-induced-attach-lag' and add alert for NVMe queue depth + attach_latency correlation. Owner: Miguel Ortega. Deadline: 2026-03-21.
Customer communication: Riley Chen to draft incident summary and recommended platform + customer configuration changes; schedule review call 2026-03-15.
